Haft Sitora (Seven Stars) is a young and ambitious team from Tajikistan united by curiosity about space, science, and innovation. Like seven stars forming one constellation, each member brings unique strengths, ideas, and perspectives.

We are passionate about exploring challenges, learning from scientific research, and transforming our ideas into meaningful solutions. Our goal is to think beyond boundaries and contribute to a future where space exploration becomes safer and more accessible.
summary:
ORBITAL MEDIC is an interactive web-based platform designed to help astronauts monitor their health during space missions. It combines an interactive 3D human body, physiological health indicators, visual data tracking, and space-related medical information.

The platform covers six areas: brain and behavior, eyes and vision, cardiovascular, respiratory, immune, and space radiation. Through a daily check-in, users can enter 14 health indicators, which are evaluated using reference ranges and displayed through three color-coded statuses: Normal, Attention, and Action Required.

Users can explore anatomical structures, review health trends, learn how spaceflight affects the human body, and access recommendations for astronauts and onboard medical personnel. Supporting space station, lunar, and Mars transit environments, ORBITAL MEDIC demonstrates how visual health monitoring could contribute to safer long-duration space exploration.
details:
1. Project Overview

ORBITAL MEDIC is an interactive web-based health monitoring platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 challenge, "Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts."

The project aims to demonstrate how astronauts could monitor their physiological condition, understand potential health risks, and access relevant guidance during space missions, particularly when communication with Earth is delayed.

2. How It Works

The central feature is an interactive 3D human body that users can rotate, zoom in on, and explore. Selecting an anatomical structure opens an information panel containing its name, function, potential effects of spaceflight, relevant health indicators, and guidance for astronauts and onboard medical personnel.

The platform focuses on six areas:

  • Brain & Behavior
  • Eyes & Vision
  • Cardiovascular System
  • Respiratory System
  • Immune System
  • Space Radiation

Through a daily health check-in, users can manually enter 14 health indicators, including heart rate, blood pressure, blood oxygen saturation, glucose, body temperature, sleep, mood, eye pressure, radiation exposure, bone density changes, and muscle fatigue.

The platform evaluates the available values against reference ranges and assigns three color-coded statuses: Normal, Attention, and Action Required. Each system has an overall status based on its indicators. Users can also explore historical graphs, health explanations, measurement methods, and suggested next steps.

Additional features include three mission environments (Space Station, Moon, and Mars Transit), a health routine section, a space hazards section, and English and Russian language support.

3. Benefits and Intended Impact

Spaceflight exposes astronauts to health challenges associated with microgravity, radiation, isolation, altered environments, and limited access to immediate medical assistance.

ORBITAL MEDIC addresses these challenges through a visual approach to health information. Instead of presenting isolated numbers in conventional tables, it connects physiological indicators to an interactive anatomical model.

Its intended impact is to improve health awareness, make complex medical information easier to interpret, and demonstrate how monitoring interfaces could support communication between astronauts and medical personnel during long-duration missions.

4. Technology and Development

The final version uses Next.js 16, React 19, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, and Three.js for interactive 3D visualization. OrbitControls enables rotation and navigation around the anatomical model.

The 3D assets come from open anatomical resources, including Z-Anatomy, BodyParts3D, and the Human Reference Atlas. The project uses Claude Code (Anthropic) as an AI-assisted development tool for code generation, debugging, and preparation of 3D assets. The application is hosted on Vercel, and its source code is available on GitHub.

The interface is designed for desktop and mobile browsers and uses a responsive layout.

5. Creativity and Design Approach

Our main creative decision was to make the human body the primary interface for health monitoring. Users can interact directly with anatomical structures instead of navigating exclusively through numerical dashboards.

We also introduced a mission-dependent risk presentation, historical health visualization, separate guidance for astronauts and medical personnel, and a Bio-Monitor vest concept representing a wearable monitoring system.

6. Research and Limitations

The project incorporates information from NASA's Human Research Program and other open anatomical and scientific resources.

The demonstration contains simulated data representing a 14-day mission. These values are not real astronaut medical records. Some thresholds are standard adult reference ranges, while others are illustrative demonstration thresholds or comparisons with baseline values.

ORBITAL MEDIC is a prototype, not a clinically validated diagnostic system. It currently relies on manual data entry, does not connect directly to medical sensors, and does not permanently store user entries. Specialized examinations, including blood tests and eye imaging, require separate medical equipment.
